paper: Accommodation Goes Both Ways: Studying Linguistic Convergence Between Humans and Language Models
secondary_reference: French, D'Mello & von der Wense (2024), A Study of Linguistic Alignment in Dialogue Systems, HuCLLM: shuffled-response baseline design
metric_source: Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil & Lee (2011); Eq. 1 of Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil, Lee, Pang & Kleinberg (2012), implemented in regesh.bonding.synchrony.CoordinationCounts
scope: Pre-outcome locked scoped replication on a different model, corpus role and lexicon; direction and contrasts comparable, absolute levels not

data.name: DailyDialog
data.citation: Li, Su, Shen, Li, Cao & Niu (2017), IJCNLP
data.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (research use; derived short excerpts stored in items.jsonl and rows.jsonl for audit; raw data kept outside git)
data.original_url_status_2026-10-25: domain parked (HTML sale page, 980 bytes); Wayback Machine copies unreachable through the session proxy
data.mirror_description: ParlAI (Facebook AI) JSON-lines conversion of the original release, archive dated 2018-12-11, same 11118 train dialogues in the original tokenized text

text_normalization: Straight apostrophes; 'X ' s|t|m|d|ll|re|ve|em|clock' rejoined to contractions; space before , . ! ? ; : removed; whitespace collapsed. Applied to contexts, human replies and model replies before measurement.
cut_rule: k = cut_points[int(SHA256('{seed}:cut:{normalized dialogue}'), 16) % 3]; context = turns 1..k, u1 = turn k, human u2 = turn k+1; dialogue dropped if k+1 > turns
duplicates: exact duplicate normalized dialogues dropped, first occurrence kept
selection: first 200 eligible dialogues by ascending SHA256('{seed}:select:{index}:{normalized dialogue}'); no model output inspected
system_prompt: You are the second speaker in a casual two-person conversation. Reply with one short natural line.
bounded_sentence: Keep your own natural wording; do not echo or mirror the other speaker's phrasing.
bounded_sentence_source: derived from the platform mid-range coordination target (regesh.bonding.synchrony.HUMAN_CONVERGENCE_REFERENCE)
message_roles: speaker of turn k -> user, replier -> assistant, relative to the cut; even k means the replier opened the dialogue and the first context message is an assistant turn
decode_seed_rule: seed + item index (0-based position in items.jsonl), shared by both conditions of an item
condition_order: plain first for even item index, bounded first for odd index
reply_cleanup: first non-empty output line; leading speaker label (A:, B:, Speaker 1:, User:, ...) and surrounding quotes removed; then text_normalization; provider error or blank output counts as an empty reply and the row is kept
secondary_marker_set: all nine lexicon categories including negate (Blevins' LIWC mean includes negation)
lexicon: regesh.bonding.synchrony.LEXICON: authored open closed-class list, NOT the LIWC 2007 dictionary
primary_statistic: aggregated_3: mean over markers the targets exhibit at least once of C^m(reply set -> u1), each response set treated as one speaker over all 200 exchanges
bootstrap_design: paired item bootstrap: the same resampled items for human, plain and bounded sets; percentile 95% intervals for set means and for plain-human, bounded-human, plain-bounded

content_proxy.source: top frequent tokens of the 200 selected u1 texts excluding every lexicon function word; ties alphabetical
content_proxy.declared_as: WordNet-free, POS-free substitute for Blevins' top-100 noun lemmas

lsm: Ireland et al. (2011) over all nine lexicon categories, mean over items (all items, and non-empty replies)
endpoints: direction and size of plain-minus-human convergence gap versus published LIWC mean +.033 (eight-marker mean derived from Table 2: +.021)
content proxy plain versus human versus published noun .442 vs .141
whether the bounded instruction reduces the gap without emptying replies (empty fraction, reply length)

published_reference.setting: WildChat English, ChatGPT GPT-3.5/4 turns vs user turns; DailyDialog and Ubuntu human-human; LIWC 2007 categories; top-100 WordNet-filtered noun lemmas
published_reference.note: Table 2 Ubuntu LIWC means are .022/.020; the .040/.038 sometimes quoted are its quant column. DailyDialog scores average both speakers over all turns.
published_reference.comparison_warning: Different model, corpus role, lexicon and noun proxy; no same-estimand effect size
